title: LavaPHP CLI envelope
description: The vocabulary every `lava <command> --json` output shares: the envelope, the problem object, and a source location. Each command's schema references `$defs/envelope` and then constrains only `data` — which is why an agent can parse one shape for every command and read a problem from any of them, boot report, HTTP body, or check section alike.

envelope.description: One command invocation's complete result, on stdout, as a single JSON object.

schema.description: The contract this output obeys. The file naming it is docs/schemas/<schema>.json, and the trailing /N is frozen: a breaking change to a payload means a new /N, never an edit.

command.description: The command that produced it, as typed (a subcommand reports its command, so `lava features resolve` reports `features`).

status.description: ok exits 0. failed exits 1 for a problem or a red result, and 2 for a malformed invocation.

data.description: The command's payload. Its keys are promised for EVERY exit path — including a failed boot — so a consumer never branches on a shape it was told was stable.

problems.description: Every problem found, in the order to act on them: fatals before warnings, and within each severity a fix that starts with 'Run: ' before one that needs judgement. Empty on a clean run.

problem.description: A diagnosis an agent can act on without a second round trip: what is wrong, where, with what input, and the imperative fix.

code.description: Stable identifier, 1:1 with a Problem class and catalogued in docs/problem-codes.md. Branch on this, never on the message.

problem.description: What is wrong, naming the failing input.

fix.description: The imperative fix. A fix starting with 'Run: ' names a command that resolves it, which is why `lava check` sorts those first within a severity.

context.description: The exact values involved, so the diagnosis is checkable without re-deriving them.

source.description: Where the offending declaration lives, when it is a file. Null for problems about the environment or a request.

severity.description: fatal fails the run (exit 1); warn is reported and exits 0 unless --strict escalates it.

source.description: A file and 1-based line, formatted as file:line everywhere it is rendered.
